item.title: Drill 2026-10-15: decode-instruction (inc via FF /0)
item.description:
Decode-one-instruction drill
Windows x64. Decode this instruction:
48 FF 45 F8
What is the assembly? What does it do to memory, and where exactly?
Answer: inc qword ptr [rbp-8]
- 48 = REX.W (64-bit operand size). FF is the "group 5" opcode; the ModRM reg field is an extension: /0 = INC, /1 = DEC (/2 = call, /4 = jmp, /6 = push). - ModRM 45 = 01 000 101: mod=01 (disp8 follows), reg=000 (/0 = INC), rm=101 (rbp as base). - F8 is the signed disp8 = -8, so the 8-byte value at rbp-8 is incremented in place (read-modify-write, no register loaded).
